# Introduction

This file is used to conduct ordinal regression analysis on the survey responses of Recreational fishers from the SELTMP in 2025. Regressions test trends between responses to ranked 1-10 questions, such as support for MPAs, against demographic information on the respondents such as education level

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# R Setup & housekeeping
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
	echo = TRUE,
	include = TRUE,
	message = FALSE,
	warning = FALSE)

rm(list=ls())
objects()
```

```{r}
# Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(ordinal)   # clm() for models and nominal_test()
library(MASS)      # polr() for Brant test
library(brant)     # Brant test for proportional odds
library(car)       # Model comparisons and diagnostics
library(emmeans)   # Marginal means if needed
```

# 1. Prepare data

```{r}
# Import Raw Data sheet
raw_data <- read_excel(here::here("Data/SELTMP-2025-GBR-surveydataset_v1-0_RecFishingCLUSTERS_RyanW-Oct-22-2026.xlsx"), sheet = "Raw_Data")

#glimpse(raw_data)
```

```{r}
# Filter Data for only Rec Fishers
fisher_data <- raw_data |> filter(Are_you_a_Rec_Fisher == 1)
nrow(fisher_data)
```

```{r}
# Option A: Set up predictor variables as factors 
data <- fisher_data %>%
  transmute(
    inter_zoning = as.integer(inter_zoning),
    educ = as.integer(educ)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(inter_zoning), !is.na(educ)) %>%
  mutate(
    inter_zoning = factor(inter_zoning, ordered = TRUE, levels = 1:10),
    educ = factor(educ, ordered = FALSE))

# Check response distribution
table(data$inter_zoning)
```

```{r}
# Option B: Set up predictor variables as numeric
data <- fisher_data %>%
  transmute(
    inter_zoning = as.integer(inter_zoning),
    educ = as.integer(educ)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(inter_zoning), !is.na(educ)) %>%
  mutate(
    inter_zoning = factor(inter_zoning, ordered = TRUE, levels = 1:10),
    educ = as.numeric(as.character(educ)))

fisher_data <- fisher_data %>% mutate(educ = as.numeric(as.character(educ)))

# Check response distribution
table(data$inter_zoning)
```

# 2. Ordered logit model (proportional odds model)

```{r}
# Model 1: education as a single predictor
m_ord <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = data, link = "logit")
summary(m_ord)

# To examine multiple predictors:
#m_ord_full <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ + age_group + gender, data = data, link = "logit")
#summary(m_ord_full)
```

# 3. Check proportional odds / parallel slopes assumption

```{r}
# Option A: nominal_test() from ordinal package
# This is the standard check for parallel slopes in clm()
nominal_test(m_ord)

# If it is significant, the proportional odds assumption is likely violated.
```

```{r}
# Option B: Brant test from MASS::polr
m_p <- MASS::polr(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = data, Hess = TRUE)
brant(m_p)

# Note:
# - If using clm(), the nominal_test() is usually the better direct check.
# - If using polr(), use brant()
```

# 4. LR test for overall model significance

```{r}
# Null model: intercept only
m_null <- clm(inter_zoning ~ 1, data = data, link = "logit")

# Log-likelihoods
ll_null <- as.numeric(logLik(m_null))
ll_model <- as.numeric(logLik(m_ord))

# LR statistic
lr_stat <- 2 * (ll_model - ll_null)

# Degrees of freedom difference
df_diff <- attr(logLik(m_ord), "df") - attr(logLik(m_null), "df")

# p-value
p_value <- pchisq(lr_stat, df = df_diff, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Report (if significant the model fits the data better than the null hypothesis)
data.frame(
  Model = "Ordered logit vs intercept only",
  LR = lr_stat,
  df = df_diff,
  p_value = p_value
)
```

# 5. AIC/BIC for model comparison

```{r}
AIC(m_ord)
BIC(m_ord)

# compare with null model
AIC(m_null)
BIC(m_null)

# Note: Model with lower score is better 
# - AIC is more useful for small sample sizes and complex models. Focused on prediction
# - BIC is more useful for large sample sizes, but penalizes having more parameters. Focused on theory 
```

# 6. If proportional odds assumption is violated: Generalized ordered logit model

(allows the effect of a predictor to vary across the cutpoints/thresholds (i.e., non-parallel slopes))

```{r}
# Option A: run earlier code chunks to ensure predictors numerical
  m_gen <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = data, link = "logit")
  summary(m_gen)
  
# If multiple predictors:
# m_gen_full <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ + age_group + gender, data = dat, link = "logit",
# nominal = ~ educ + age_group)
# summary(m_gen_full)
```
```{r}
# Option B: run earlier code chunks to ensure predictors are factors 
# (WILL HAVE TO FIX THIS LATER BY COLLAPSING DATA INTO FEWER CATEGORIES)
  m_gen <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = data, link = "logit", nominal = ~ educ)
  summary(m_gen)
  
# If multiple predictors:
# m_gen_full <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ + age_group + gender, data = dat, link = "logit",
# nominal = ~ educ + age_group)
# summary(m_gen_full)
```

# 7. Compare proportional odds model to generalized model

```{r}
# Test whether the unrestricted (generalized) model is significantly better w/LR test:
ll_ord <- as.numeric(logLik(m_ord))
ll_gen <- as.numeric(logLik(m_gen))

lr_gen <- 2 * (ll_gen - ll_ord)
df_gen <- attr(logLik(m_gen), "df") - attr(logLik(m_ord), "df")
p_gen <- pchisq(lr_gen, df = df_gen, lower.tail = FALSE)

data.frame(
  Model = "Generalized ordered logit vs ordered logit",
  LR = lr_gen,
  df = df_gen,
  p_value = p_gen
)
```

# 8. Test assumptions

```{r}
# Use LR test to compare to null model:
ll_null <- as.numeric(logLik(m_null))
ll_gen <- as.numeric(logLik(m_gen))

lr_gen <- 2 * (ll_gen - ll_null)
df_gen <- attr(logLik(m_gen), "df") - attr(logLik(m_null), "df")
p_gen <- pchisq(lr_gen, df = df_gen, lower.tail = FALSE)

data.frame(
  Model = "Generalized ordered logit vs ordered logit",
  LR = lr_gen,
  df = df_gen,
  p_value = p_gen
)
```

```{r}
# nominal_test() to determine if non-parallel slope terms are needed
nominal_test(m_gen)

# Compare AIC and BIC values
AIC(m_gen)
BIC(m_gen)
AIC(m_null)
BIC(m_null)
```
